opus.why: One-word typo fix and a one-line commit message. Nothing to reason about.

fable.why: One-character typo fix in a 9-line component plus a one-line commit message. No judgment involved; any model produces the identical result.

opus.why: A stale-response race in a debounced async effect. The fix needs cancellation or an ignore flag, and the reproducing test needs fake timers and promises that resolve out of order. Sonnet can do it but needs room to think.

fable.why: Classic stale-response race in a debounced hook; the fix (cancelled flag or AbortController in cleanup) is well known. Writing a test that deterministically reproduces out-of-order resolution with fake timers and deferred promises takes some care, so high effort on Sonnet rather than medium.

opus.why: Reading the log is fairly easy: the rotated key wasn't reloaded, recovery came only from an accidental OOM restart, and the duplicate-charge guard fired. The payment-incident copy customers will read needs careful, trust-preserving wording, and that is where a quality drop would show.

fable.why: Needs the correct causal read (key rotated, service kept key_v6 until an unrelated OOM restart reloaded v7, retries hit the duplicate-charge guard) and then two audiences of copy, one customer-facing. Sonnet at high effort gets both the diagnosis and short plain-language copy right; Opus adds nothing on 3-4 sentences.

opus.why: Creative judgment the audience sees: pacing critique, a cold-open hook that has to land in the first 5 seconds, and thumbnail prompts that match the new hook.

fable.why: Audience-facing creative work: pacing diagnosis across beats, a cold-open rewrite that must hook in 5 seconds, and thumbnail prompts that carry visual judgment. This is exactly where a weaker model's output reads flatter and the owner would notice.

opus.why: Contrast math is mechanical: white on #3BA3F0 fails AA, so Option B wins. Then sync the brand book and tokens.css and write a short client rationale. Sonnet handles this well.

fable.why: The contrast decision is computable (Option A primary fails AA with white text, both accents fail with white, which must be flagged), but the deliverable is brand-book copy, token edits, and a client-facing rationale. Brand judgment plus client wording justifies Opus; medium effort is enough since the math and edits are bounded.

opus.why: Continues the multi-vehicle schema change: a migration that creates the table and backfills it, plus API doc updates. Moderate care is needed so the data migration is correct.

fable.why: Continues a schema-architecture change: new vehicles table, FK, backfill migration preserving existing data, endpoint rename with compatibility considerations, and matching API docs. Migration mistakes are costly and hard to reverse, so Opus at high.

opus.why: Check the numbers against the CSV: South actually fell 2.3% and the total is about +8.2%. Then fix the table and write an honest headline. Simple arithmetic and a short line of copy.

fable.why: Reconcile a slide table with a CSV: South actually fell (288k to 281.5k), the total is about +8.2% not +10.1%, and the title must be rewritten honestly. Arithmetic plus a short truthful headline; Sonnet at medium does this correctly.

opus.why: A simple validation script plus two short, tightly constrained i2v prompts written from clear beat descriptions.

fable.why: The checker script is trivial, but the second half is authoring image-to-video prompts from beat descriptions with mood, framing, and subtle camera moves. That is visual creative output the owner ships, so Opus; medium effort since the beats are short and well specified.

opus.why: A public LinkedIn post in the owner's own voice. The audience reads the final copy, so writing quality matters even though summarizing the article is easy.

fable.why: Final published copy in the user's voice with explicit style constraints (no filler, no emoji) distilled from a short article. Extraction is easy; the post's tone and tightness are what the audience reads, so Opus, with medium effort sufficient for a short post.
